title: The categorical palette fails colour-blind separation, and small marks need a ramp that does not
foundBy: consumer report (host): an application consuming this package, moving from 0.2.0 to 0.3.0, with measurements and reproduction steps
details:
A consumer draws node-link diagrams over a model of 353 nodes and 411 edges, at dots of 3 to 5 pixels and lines of 1 pixel. They report that `--color-cat-1..10` does not hold at that mark size, and ask for a second ramp rather than hand-rolling one downstream.

Measured with the palette validator from the `dataviz` skill, which runs five checks: lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair separation under colour-blind simulation, normal-vision separation, and contrast against the surface.

Nine of the ten base slots fail four of the five checks on the dark surface. Separation under deuteranopia falls to 1.8 between `#6ab0d4` and `#c489c9`, and normal-vision separation falls to 12.2 between `#4fb3a6` and `#6f93c9`, under a floor of 15. The light set fails the same way.

The `-mid` sub-shades are the obvious alternative and they also fail. Separation under deuteranopia is 1.8 between `#0ea5e9` and `#d946ef` on the dark set, and 2.5 between `#0369a1` and `#a21caf` on the light set.

The consumer has nine categories, and reports that every nine-hue set they tested merges a pair under deuteranopia or protanopia. They therefore ask for eight slots and a defined neutral, which matches the documented rule that a ninth category folds to "Other" rather than becoming a generated hue.

The proposal is `--color-graph-1..8` for small marks, leaving `--color-cat-*` untouched for bar charts, with `--color-graph-other` aliased to `--color-structural`. The light values are `#2a78d6`, `#e26432`, `#189d6e`, `#bb7f00`, `#cc6c90`, `#008300`, `#4a3aa7` and `#e34948`. The dark values are `#3987e5`, `#d95926`, `#199e70`, `#c98500`, `#d55181`, `#008300`, `#9085e9` and `#e66767`.

Those values pass all five checks in both themes. Worst colour-blind separation is 8.7 light and 8.4 dark, worst normal-vision separation is 16.6 light and 19.3 dark, and every slot clears 3:1 contrast. The light surface tested was `#ffffff` and the dark surface `#0f1620`.

Upgrading does not escape the problem. `src/styles/tokens.css` is byte-identical between the `v0.3.0` tag and main at 8ada6d1, and no `--color-graph-*` token exists.

notes.text: Every figure the reporter gave was re-run against the same validator before filing, and all five palettes reproduce exactly, including the two weaknesses they disclosed themselves. Those are a tritan separation of 3.7 between the proposed light slots 3 and 4, and a colour-blind margin of 8.4 to 8.7 that clears the floor of 8 with little room. The second means the ramp needs documenting as requiring secondary encoding, such as a legend, a label or a hover, rather than as safe on colour alone.

The report frames `--color-cat-*` as a good bar-chart palette that is poor for small marks. The measurements do not support the first half. A deuteranopia separation of 1.8 means two slots are the same colour, and a larger mark does not separate them. So adding a second ramp leaves the existing one failing for everyone who uses it, which makes this a wider decision than an additive token.

Against that, the validator is a tool from an external skill rather than a gate this repository adopted, and there is no palette gate here. `src/styles/tokens.css` records a review of the palette on 2026-08-27 against a real 1,366-event strip in both themes. Whether these thresholds become the standard is a decision rather than a correction.

The report cited a seven-character sha for main to support its claim that the palette is unchanged. That commit was a ledger commit on an unmerged branch, made the day the report was written, and it touched no stylesheet. This record cites the tag comparison instead. Recorded because a wrong sha that still resolves against this repository passes the freshness gate while meaning something else.

The reporter withdrew the framing that this is a small-mark problem, and named the mechanism instead. What separates the two regimes is which pairs of hues can ever touch. A bar, line or stacked chart only asks whether one series is distinct from its neighbour. A node-link diagram asks it of every pair, because any category can land beside any other.

Measured on the base palette against `#0f1620`, comparing adjacent pairs with all pairs. At five slots, adjacent separation passes at 9.4 while all-pairs separation falls to 0.9 between `#9e90cc` and `#6f93c9` under protanopia. At seven slots, adjacent warns at 6.4 and all-pairs stays at 0.9. At nine slots, adjacent fails at 1.8 and all-pairs falls to 0.5 between `#c489c9` and `#9e90cc`. Every figure was reproduced before this note was written.

Worse, the palette misses the normal-vision floor at two slots. `--color-cat-1` and `--color-cat-2` separate by 12.2 against a floor of 15, and both sit below the chroma floor. That is the first two series of any chart drawn with this palette.

This explains why the worked examples never surfaced it. `patterns/Chart.md` demonstrates a bar chart, a sankey diagram and a line chart, which are all adjacent-pair forms at series counts where the adjacent column still passes or warns. The gap was invisible by construction rather than by oversight. The legend example in that same document paints with `theme.categorical[0]` and `theme.categorical[1]`, which is the pair that misses the normal-vision floor.

Two consequences for the decision. A ramp's contract states more usefully as a pair regime than as a mark size, because a consumer can tell whether any pair of their series may touch. And the scope is wider than an additive token, since the default palette misses a floor in the common case rather than only in a specialised one.

One distinction to carry into the spec decision, because it splits the question in two. The floors themselves, 15 for normal vision and 8 for colour-blind separation, are the validator's policy and are arguable. A protan separation of 0.9, or 0.5, is not a threshold question. At that distance two hues are the same colour for those readers under any standard.

So rejecting the thresholds does not dispose of the palette question. It changes which parts survive. The all-pairs collapse survives on its own terms, and the two-slot normal-vision miss depends on accepting a floor of 15.

Scope decided by the owner. Each palette carries a stated contract and is held to that contract rather than to the other's.

`--color-cat-*` is safe where only adjacent series meet, which is a bar, line or stacked chart. It is fixed only as far as that contract requires. `--color-graph-*` is safe where any pair may meet, which is a node-link diagram, a scatter or a small multiple. It carries eight slots and a neutral.

The separation floors are adopted as this project's standard, and a check enforces them so neither palette drifts. A contract without a gate becomes a comment nobody re-runs, and this repository keeps finding that a check which cannot run where the work happens reports its failure to whoever merges.

Two consequences to settle while writing the contracts. The adjacent contract cannot claim ten slots, because the palette passes adjacent separation at five, warns at seven and fails at nine. Either the failing slots move or the documented count is capped. And the pair of slots that misses the normal-vision floor sits inside the adjacent contract at any count, so it needs a decision either way.

Two rules for the contract, supplied by the reporter from five real drawings rather than from principle.

An empty category is absent rather than neutral. Four of their five drawings populate fewer than eight categories, and an unpopulated one draws no mark and no legend row. The neutral is only ever for the overflow past eight. Without saying so, an implementer reaches for the neutral to mean empty and the two meanings collide.

Slots are assigned from a fixed declared order, never by size or rank. The smallest populated category differs in every one of their drawings, so a rule that folds the smallest would move the neutral between drawings and change a category's colour depending on which drawing is open. Colour follows the entity rather than its rank, and the neutral always takes the same ninth position.

Their taxonomy declares nine categories. All nine appear together in one drawing of the five, where the ninth carries two elements out of 442. So eight slots and a neutral cost that consumer two marks on one drawing and nothing on the other four.
